title: Monthly Rent and Care Fee Billing Standard (Assisted Living)
content:
**Business Office billing standard for the Assisted Living Residency and Care Agreement.**

### Clauses in force

1. **Absences.** Rent and care fees continue during an absence; only the care fee is relieved, and only through the absence care credit.
2. **Status.** Rent and care fee charges may be posted only while the residency is in active, on leave or notice given status. A residency in pending admission, vacated, closed or cancelled status takes no rent or care fee charge.

### Retired clauses — no longer in force

The two clauses below, in their original wording, are no longer in force and have been superseded by the current basis:

- "Rent and the care level fee are billed in advance on the fee due day of each calendar month for the whole month: rent at the contracted monthly rent and the care fee at the monthly care fee of the level billed."
- "The move-in month, the month of a level or rent change and the month in which fees end are prorated: the daily amount is the monthly amount divided by the actual number of days in that calendar month, multiplied by the days billed counted inclusive of both ends, and rounded once to the cent half up" — with its two expressions, prorated rent being the contracted monthly rent multiplied by the days billed and divided by the days in the month, and prorated care being the monthly care fee multiplied by the days billed and divided by the days in the month, each rounded to the cent.

### Points of judgement

| Residency status | Rent or care fee charge may be posted |
|---|---|
| Active | Yes |
| On leave | Yes — rent and care fees continue during the absence |
| Notice given | Yes |
| Pending admission, vacated, closed, cancelled | No |

The move-in month, the month of a level or rent change and the month in which fees end are prorated: the daily amount is the monthly amount divided by the actual number of days in that calendar month, multiplied by the days billed counted inclusive of both ends, and rounded once to the cent half up.
